$$
[1,5]=[1,2]\cup [2,5],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $3$ | $7$ |

activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Areas With the Trapezoidal Rule

feedback.problem:
Using the trapezoidal rule with the partition

$$
[-3,2]=[-3,-1]\cup [-1,0]\cup [0,2],
$$

approximate the area under the curve of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ whose data is given in the table below.

| $x$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $2$ | $4$ | $8$ | $6$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's plot what this function might look like, using the values given in the table.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14055663/assets/25dc419eb5711b0d990909c611a6eacb2754285fb45dc0d969207e63dc09ba12.png)

We've drawn some trapezoids to help calculate our trapezoidal rule sum. By calculating the area of each trapezoid, we obtain the following approximation for our area $A:$

$$
A≈\overset{1\text{st trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-3)+f(-1)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{1}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{2\text{nd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(-1)+f(0)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{2}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}+\overset{3\text{rd trapezoid}}{\overset{⏞}{[\,\frac{\overset{\text{bases}}{\overset{⏞}{f(0)+f(2)}}}{2}\,\cdot \,{{Δ{x}_{3}}_{⏟}}_{\text{height}}\,]}}
$$

Substituting the appropriate numbers into the above expression gives

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈\frac{2+4}{2}\cdot (-1-(-3))+\frac{4+8}{2}\cdot (0-(-1))+\frac{8+6}{2}\cdot (2-0) \\  & =3\cdot 2+6\cdot 1+7\cdot 2 \\  & =6+6+14 \\  & =26\,.\end{aligned}
$$
